title: Spare Parts Dispatch & Export Clearance: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
workplace_track: Export Logistics & Incoterms 2020 (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DDP)
description: Differentiate finished past time from ongoing status up to the present when updating foreign dealerships on consignments, customs clearances, and delivery milestones.
learning_objectives: Distinguish Present Perfect with indefinite/unfinished time from Past Simple with definite past dates
Communicate accurate logistics milestones to overseas truck dealers

questions.prompt: Our logistics coordinator _____ the bill of lading to the Australian dealer yesterday afternoon.

explanations.correct: With a specific completed time reference ('yesterday afternoon'), English strictly requires Past Simple ('emailed').
explanations.wrong_A: Present Perfect cannot co-occur with specific past time indicators like 'yesterday afternoon'.
explanations.wrong_C: Present Continuous refers to current or future scheduled action, not yesterday's finished dispatch.
explanations.wrong_D: Present Perfect Continuous cannot be used with a closed past time adverbial.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech speakers often overuse Present Perfect when an action feels recent, saying 'has emailed yesterday'. In English, 'yesterday' always triggers Past Simple.

questions.prompt: We _____ with this Polish defense distributor since 2017, and our partnership remains very strong.

explanations.correct: For a state or action starting in the past and continuing up to the present with 'since', Present Perfect ('have worked') is required.
explanations.wrong_A: Present Simple cannot express duration continuing from a past point to the present.
explanations.wrong_B: Present Continuous cannot be used with 'since 2017' to express long-term duration.
explanations.wrong_D: Past Simple ('worked') implies the partnership has already ended, contradicting 'remains very strong'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses Present Simple with 'od' ('Pracujeme s nimi od roku 2017'). Translating this as 'We work with them since 2017' is one of the most frequent Czenglish errors.

questions.prompt: "_____ the sea freight forwarder yet regarding the delayed shipping container?"

explanations.correct: 'Yet' in inquiries about unconfirmed actions up to the present requires Present Perfect ('Have you contacted').
explanations.wrong_B: Double past error: auxiliary 'did' cannot take past form 'contacted'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses simple past ('Už jsi kontaktoval...?'). In English, 'yet' with an open time frame requires Present Perfect.

questions.prompt: The container vessel carrying ten Tatra 4x4 cabins _____ in Hamburg two days ago.

explanations.correct: The time expression 'two days ago' specifies a completed past point, demanding Past Simple ('docked').
explanations.wrong_A: 'Ago' always demands Past Simple; Present Perfect ('has docked') is incorrect.
explanations.wrong_B: Present Perfect Continuous is incompatible with 'two days ago'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'is docked' describes current state but clashes with 'two days ago'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Time phrases with 'ago' ('před dvěma dny') in Czech use past tense; never use Present Perfect with 'ago' in English.

questions.prompt: So far this quarter, Tatra _____ twenty-four Phoenix heavy-duty tippers to Scandinavia.

explanations.correct: 'So far this quarter' refers to an unfinished time period up to now, requiring Present Perfect ('has delivered').
explanations.wrong_A: Past Simple would imply the quarter is finished and closed.
explanations.wrong_B: Present Simple denotes general routine, not cumulative accomplishments to date.
explanations.wrong_D: Past Continuous implies an interrupted past background action, not a total count.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech says 'Zatím v tomto čtvrtletí dodala' with past tense. In English, 'so far' strongly triggers Present Perfect.

questions.prompt: When _____ the official purchase order for the spare swing half-axles?

explanations.correct: Questions beginning with 'When' ask for a specific point in time and therefore require Past Simple ('did the customer sign').
explanations.wrong_A: 'When' questions cannot use Present Perfect because they ask for a specific point in the past.
explanations.wrong_C: Missing auxiliary verb 'did' in direct question word order.
explanations.wrong_D: Double past error: auxiliary 'did' takes base form 'sign', not 'signed'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czechs frequently ask 'When have you signed...?' which is ungrammatical in standard English; always ask 'When did you sign...?'.

questions.prompt: Our sales director is away from the office; he _____ to Abu Dhabi to attend the military vehicle expo.

explanations.correct: 'Has gone' means he has traveled there and is still there now (away from office).
explanations.wrong_A: 'Has been' means he went and has already returned.
explanations.wrong_B: 'went to' does not explain the present result ('is away right now') as effectively without time reference.
explanations.wrong_C: 'was gone' denotes past absence rather than current whereabouts.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses 'odjel' for both situations; English differentiates 'has been' (returned) from 'has gone' (still there).

questions.prompt: In May 2024, our procurement department _____ a new long-term supply agreement for Paccar engines.

explanations.correct: 'In May 2024' specifies a past closed period, requiring Past Simple ('negotiated').
explanations.wrong_B: Present Perfect cannot accompany past calendar dates like 'In May 2024'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Whenever a past month or year is stated, always select Past Simple, never Present Perfect.

questions.prompt: I can confirm that the export customs documents _____ already _____ by the financial authority.

explanations.correct: Present Perfect Passive ('have already been cleared') expresses current validity and completed status.
explanations.wrong_A: 'were clear' is active or adjectival and does not represent the passive action of clearance.
explanations.wrong_B: 'are cleared' is less natural with 'already' when confirming recent completion.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses passive participle or active reflexive ('už byly procleny' or 'už se proclily'). English technical emails favor Present Perfect Passive.

questions.prompt: Our technical service team _____ any unresolved customer claims this month.

explanations.correct: 'This month' is an ongoing time period, so Present Perfect ('has not received') is required.
explanations.wrong_A: Double past error: auxiliary 'did' takes base verb 'receive', not 'received'.
explanations.wrong_D: Passive voice 'was not received' would mean the team itself was not received.

questions.cz_learning_point: When the time period ('this month', 'this week', 'today') is still ongoing, English uses Present Perfect.
